traditional.duration_provenance: KB benchmark anchor: Contact Center Phase 1 (Service Cloud + Agentforce + telephony) ~12-14 weeks. Adjusted up to 14-20 week baseline for: 12 epics (4 L, 5 M), 4 external API integrations, 4 custom LWCs, regulatory/compliance overlay. Risk adders: +15% Unknown API contracts (E04, E05); +10% regulatory compliance overlay (allergen P0, Shield); -5% brownfield offset (existing Service Cloud org). Net +20% high-end adder → 14-23 weeks wall-clock. Native AFCC telephony (Salesforce-owned infrastructure, no BYOT/OEM) removes third-party provisioning risk and lead-time uncertainty. Source: model-training-data (Benchmark Disclaimer applies).
traditional.capacity_summary: ~3.0 FTE program-average (14-24 weeks wall-clock; peaks ~4 FTE during Phase 2 build)

roster.justification: End-to-end design authority: Service Cloud Voice architecture, Omni-Channel config, Console layout, compliance/Shield overlay. Owns all integration design decisions. Cannot offshore — tight iteration with Walmart platform team (OMS/LMD/Subway API contracts).

Critical-path integration build: Order Lookup LWC + OMS/Subway API callouts (E04), Driver LWC + LMD un-batch API (E05). Both are Unknown-confidence L epics with unresolved API contracts — senior required, onshore for close iteration with Walmart API owners (Michelle Fultz, Edwin Ortiz).

Volume build pod: Complaint intake LWC (E06), Item Signal form (E07), allergen Flow (E06), callback/SLA Flow (E09), Console layout config (E03 sub-tabs). Standard-complexity M items well-suited to offshore delivery. Paired with senior Developer in Phase 2.

Test coverage: 4 IVR paths × 4 inquiry categories × all LWC components. Allergen P0 path requires independent QA verification (regulatory). UAT coordination with Walmart QA team. Offshore QA is appropriate for this scope — no regulated data-emit that requires onshore.

Delivery coordination across 9+ team touchpoints (Walmart: Troy/Jeff/Surojit/Michelle/Edwin/Brayden, Salesforce Voice/Platform Eng, Compliance/Legal TBD). Half-time on a single-workstream engagement. Onshore for client relationship management.

Salesforce Voice / telephony specialist: toll-free number provisioning, Amazon Connect OEM vs BYOT decision, IVR Flow build (E01), Omni-Channel routing config (E02). Fractional specialist consumed in Phases 1-2 only — distinct expertise from general SA.
Agent training support + go-live readiness (E12). WFM/CES owns the training curriculum, but PS supports the training delivery design. Light fractional engagement in Phases 3-4 only.

Surojit Mukhopadhyay (Product). Must be available to unblock 12 open questions (coverage hours, API contracts, queue ownership, etc.). A named, reachable decision-maker is the primary AI-native qualification gate. Half-time cadence minimum.

Michelle Fultz (OMS/Subway API adapter) + Edwin Ortiz (LMD un-batch API). Both needed in Phase 2 to finalize API contracts for E04/E05. Quarter-time but their responsiveness is the critical path for the Unknown-confidence L epics.
Walmart QA team + pilot store associates (2 CT Subway stores). UAT requires in-store voice testing — PS cannot substitute. Training delivery also requires Brayden Wood / WFM participation.

Must supply: call recording disclosure script, Shield retention period, allergen on-call queue owner, Compliance acknowledgement field owner. Unstaffed Compliance side is the #1 go-live blocker after API contracts.

phases.name: Discovery & Architecture
phases.activities: Finalize API contracts (OMS/Subway/LMD/Spark), confirm open questions (coverage hours, queue owners, dedup key, complaint policy, allergen queue), telephony decision (Amazon Connect OEM vs BYOT), Solution Architecture doc, Omni-Channel + Console design, IVR Flow wireframe, dev environment setup.

phases.name: Build – P0 Core
phases.activities: IVR Flow (E01), Omni-Channel QSR skill + queues (E02), Voice Call→Case Flow + Console layout (E03), Order Lookup LWC + OMS integration (E04), Driver LWC + LMD un-batch integration (E05), Complaint intake form + Allergen P0 Flow (E06), Call recording + Shield (E08). All P0 requirements.

phases.name: Build – P1 + UAT
phases.activities: Item Signal form (E07), Callback/voicemail Flow (E09), Einstein auto-summary (E10 – optional), Reporting + data pipe (E11), warm-transfer actions (PR-14). End-to-end UAT with Walmart QA across all 4 inquiry categories + IVR paths. Defect remediation.

phases.name: Hardening, Training & Go-Live
phases.activities: Agent training (QSR voice skill: LMD codes, order-flow, driver/un-batch, complaint, item signalling). Pilot store testing – 2 CT Subway stores. Phone number publishing (Seller Center, store signage). Go/no-go gate. Production cutover. Hypercare.

quantum-leap.duration_provenance: Traditional baseline 14-24 weeks compressed by efficiency native_band (~35-40%, provisional, gated — efficiency.json). compressed_low = 14×0.60 = 8.4 → 9 weeks; compressed_high = 24×0.65 = 15.6 → 16 weeks. AI-native operating model: Intent Architect directs Agentforce agent fleet + Claude Code for build volume; senior-weighted core; agents absorb config/LWC scaffolding/test generation. Benchmark-based, provisional, not a commitment.

roster.justification: Program Lead — customer relationship, gate decisions, the plan. Half-time on a single-workstream engagement. Onshore for Walmart relationship management.

Intent Architect — owns the what/why, solution intent sign-off, coaches Walmart product owner (Surojit). Directs agent fleet for architecture decisions + integration design. Owns all open-question resolution. Onshore — tight iteration with Walmart stakeholders.

Agent Orchestrator — directs Claude Code / Agentforce agent fleet for LWC build (E03–E07), Flow automation, Apex callouts. Owns day-to-day build and technical solution. Onshore for close iteration on Unknown-confidence API integrations (E04, E05). Senior required — the two integration L epics are the critical-path hard problems the human builder owns (adjustment 1).

QA is agent-amplified (AI generates test cases, test data) but never agent-replaced — an agent cannot be the independent check on its own output. Senior QA required: allergen P0 path is regulatory, Shield audit trail is compliance-sensitive. Half-time because agents handle test generation volume; human senior handles sign-off and P0 path. Surges to full in Phase 3 hardening.

Voice/telephony fractional specialist (IVR Flow, number provisioning, Omni-Channel config). Consumed Phases 1-2 only. Fractional because Agent Orchestrator directs AI for config scaffolding; specialist needed for provisioning decision only.

QUALIFICATION GATE: AI-native compression requires a named, empowered Walmart product owner (Surojit) available daily to unblock 12 open questions within 24hrs. If this role is not committed at full availability, the AI-native lane is conditional. This is the single largest qualification risk.

Michelle Fultz + Edwin Ortiz. AI-native requires faster API contract turnaround (days not weeks) — half-time dedicated engagement from both SMEs in Phase 2. Unstaffed = critical path block regardless of lane.
Pilot store testing unchanged — AI-native doesn't remove the need for in-store voice testing.
Same as traditional — compliance inputs cannot be AI-generated.

quantum-leap.qualification_note: AI-native lane requires: (1) named empowered Walmart product owner (Surojit) available daily, (2) empowered integration SMEs with <48hr turnaround on API contract decisions, (3) AI-first mandate from Troy/Jeff. Without these commitments, this lane is conditional — achievable but not deliverable without the operating model.
quantum-leap.provisional_note: AI-native band (~35-40%) provisional until AI-native actuals accumulate; magnitude uncalibrated, diagnosis grounded (decisions/0011, decisions/0033).

delta.summary: AI-native vs traditional: 9-16 weeks vs 14-24 weeks (35-40% compression, provisional). Team: ~2.2 FTE (senior-weighted core: Intent Architect + Agent Orchestrator + half-time Program Lead + half-time senior QA) vs ~3.0 FTE (SA + 2 Developers + QA + half-PM + fractional specialists). Compression comes from: agent fleet absorbing LWC scaffolding/Flow build/test generation volume under a senior directing core; sequential hard problems taken one-at-a-time by seniors. Delta narrows or disappears if API contracts are slow to resolve — the two Unknown-confidence L epics (E04, E05) are the critical path in both lanes.

assumptions: Existing Salesforce org is on Service Cloud Enterprise or Unlimited — Service Cloud Voice licensing procurement is in progress (Open Q12).
Amazon Connect OEM is the telephony approach (not BYOT) — BYOT adds ~1-2 weeks to E01.
OMS and Subway API adapter expose REST/JSON endpoints with standard OAuth — non-REST or SOAP would escalate E04 to XL.
LMD un-batch API is a synchronous REST callout — async/event-driven would add Flow orchestration complexity to E05.
No data migration required — all existing Case/Contact data remains on the existing org.
Spanish bilingual coverage is not in scope for Phase 1 — if required, adds ~S to E02 (separate skill + overflow).
Einstein for Service (E10) is optional/Phase 2 — excluded from critical path. Included in P1 scope if licensing is confirmed.
Power BI LMD Dashboard data pipe (E11) is a scheduled export / simple connector — CRM Analytics recipe build would escalate E11 to L.
Salesforce Shield is already licensed on the Walmart org — if not, activation lead time adds to E08.
Pilot (Phase 1) is 2 CT Subway stores only — staffing for 1,300-store scale is a separate WFM exercise outside this estimate.
Client-side UAT team (Walmart QA + pilot store associates) is available in Phase 3.
Compliance/Legal resource is identified and available in Phase 1 to supply disclosure script, retention period, allergen queue ownership.
